correctness.rationale: For arbitrary difference-set parameters the normalized squared Fourier intensities have mean 1, pointwise cap k and second moment at most 1+lambda(1-1/k), with exact Cauchy deficit (1). For every s=p/2>2 the Hermite interpolant at a,a,k of t^s has strictly positive third divided difference and therefore globally majorizes t^s on [0,k] with contact exactly a and k. The extremal two-point distribution (one k, v-1 a) shares the first two moments; this reconstructs the sharp formula. Equality forces one k-contact and pointwise Cauchy saturation, hence exactly the v character rays. For s=3 the polynomial remainder factors as (t-a)^2(k-t) and yields an exact three-term nonnegative deficit. Standalone integer and rational checks confirm normalization for cyclic and noncyclic examples, but are not relied on for universal quantifiers.

originality.rationale: The highest-coverage published comparison states the exact \(p=4\) difference-set synthesis norm and defect, and expressly makes no higher-moment claim; it yields the sharp quadratic-moment input but not the all-real-\(p>4\) bound by standard endpoint interpolation. Both the specialized seven-point and previously computed thirteen-point sixth moments are strictly subsumed special cases of the general all-difference-set law, not proof of it. The inspected 2017 and 2019 harmonic tight-frame primary texts concern geometric constructions. Targeted searches did not identify an equivalent full all-real-exponent theorem. Historical equivalence under convex order or frame potentials remains a residual priority risk, so the assertion is best-knowledge, not independent historical certification.
residual_risks: An unindexed sharp convex-order or quadrature-moment theorem may subsume the elementary Hermite lifting, including its equality classification.
The already-known exact p4 deficit is not novel, and the p6 special numerical constants 37/9 and 85/16 and complement-of-singleton subgroup-hole case have been published or recorded previously.
Comparison with all possible older harmonic-frame potential inequalities cannot be exhaustive from public text search.

value.rationale: A single proof gives exact best constants for a continuum of Lp norms for every finite abelian difference set and arbitrary complex coefficients, not merely a numerical improvement in one example. All strict higher-moment maximizers are completely classified, and p6 has an exact quantitative decomposition of three independent failure mechanisms. Standard L4-to-Linfty interpolation is nonsharp, so an exact norm formula does not follow by just taking known endpoint operator norms. This provides structural harmonic-frame moment data applicable to all Singer, Paley and noncyclic Hadamard constructions.
